utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I reviewed my notes, Your Honour, and I am finished. No more questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I know that this is not customary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, well what is it you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wished to ask you, in view of the fact that the witness has been testifying now for four or five days in a row and during his cross-examination by Mr. Hannis, he provided some new information about the role of certain individuals and the relationship between the police and the army. I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to give me an opportunity to put some additional questions to him in relation to what was raised this morning and yesterday during the cross-examination by Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you give me an example?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. An example is the role of Mr. Adamovic, an example is what General Djordjevic said at that meeting on the 22nd of July; an example is the beginning of today's transcript, that certain documents were handed out at this meeting of the army and the police on the 22nd of July, and we first -- and that was the first time we heard about that, and then these plans from 1998 that were valid in 1999 as well. So it would be along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I did talk about Mr. Adamovic a little bit. As far as the documents being handed out at the first meeting, I think there was some evidence of that from Colonel Delic when he testified, so it's -- I don't know, it's not such a new topic. And as far as General Djordjevic, I don't remember me raising that issue about General Djordjevic saying something at the meeting on the 22nd of July. I don't recall what that was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was that raised by Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not Mr. Hannis, but it was an answer to his question. Mr. Hannis's question was that there was a task that was set out in the decision on the establishment of the staff, and the answer was that all of that had been stopped and -- well, there is no point in me going into that now because otherwise there's no point in asking the witness anything. As for General Delic in his testimony, I checked during the break carefully, he did talk about meetings with the MUP but at a lower level where coordination was carried out. General Delic did not mention that specific meeting on the 22nd or the 23rd of July in Pristina where everybody was present, the assistant ministers, and Generals Pavkovic and Lazarevic. He did not specifically speak about that, whereas this witness said this morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding Adamovic and Djordjevic, we discussed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's your position. Are you opposing this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You are going to have a chance to re-examine. What's your problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Everything was raised during the direct examination. We mentioned Djordjevic and Obrad Stevanovic coming to the meeting on the 22nd of July, 1998, explaining why the plan should be implemented by the police. It was during the direct, and we raised the role of Mr. Adamovic in his -- but the witness said as much as he could and said that Mr. Adamovic could be able to explain more on his role. So I'm sure that it's in direct examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's difficult to see, though, that this can prejudice you because you get the chance of the last word in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll leave it to Your Honours then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. But is it only these two matters that you oppose? What about the rest of the meeting on the 22nd of July and the question of the level of representation that we didn't have discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Are you opposed to that as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that I tried at least to cover these topics in my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very difficult to adjudicate on this kind of thing. What we'll do is we'll allow you to commence this further cross-examination, Mr. Aleksic, but please ensure that the matters you're addressing are ones which directly arise from something said in answer to questions by Mr. Hannis and not from the examination-in-chief. This isn't a second opportunity to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will follow your instructions, and I will try to act accordingly. Further cross-examination by Mr. Aleksic:

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I just have a few questions for you. Today at the beginning of the transcript on 2, line 19, until page 3, line 2, you responded to the Prosecutor's questions related to a meeting held on the 22nd and 23rd of July between the leadership of the Army of Yugoslavia and the police and you said that at that meeting documents were handed out to officers. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that what I said was that on the eve of this activity, on the 25th of July, a meeting was held, that's what I said during the course of these past few days, officers of the police and the army attended that meeting, and people were given guide-lines from this plan. And what was handed out were action documents, and people who did not know each other met there, officers from the army and the police. I cannot tell you what the exact date was because indeed it has been nine years and I cannot recall all of that, but it is certain that a meeting like that was held and I cannot say specifically when it was. Perhaps I made a mistake in saying the 22nd, maybe it was the 21st or the 23rd, and perhaps it wasn't even that same meeting, perhaps it was a different meeting, but anyway that would be about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, I'm not challenging that. There was a meeting. Yes. I'm just telling you, during these previous four days in response to different questions, and Judge Bonomy asked you about this yesterday and you gave an explicit answer, until subordination took place, you only got map extracts and this morning you said something different. That's the point of my question.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I didn't understand. I'm saying now that up until subordination only map extracts were received and after subordination maps and, order, "zapovesti," perhaps it was a slip of the tongue, perhaps I wasn't clear enough, but the fact is, that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do you mean by action documents were handed out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm saying until subordination map extracts were given for the police units that were taking part; and after that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've told us that at this meeting whenever it was towards the end of July, in the second half of July, 1998, that action documents were handed out. What were these action documents is what Mr. Aleksic wants to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I don't know what the interpretation of this was, but it actually has to do with these map extracts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In relation to this, Colonel, the Prosecutor showed you P1434 this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could that please be called up again, it is page 8 in Serbian and 18 in English. I'm just interested in the last sentence in 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you could please read it out, the last sentence, 8.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "For secret command over units, elaborate a single coded map which should be handed over to all unit commanders in extract form."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, am I right that what you, or rather, the MUP staff received and then sent further on to PJP units were extracts from this kind of coded, single, unified map that is used for coordination of activities and providing information on positions reached?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not denying that this kind of map existed in order not to have positions revealed, because it was radio transmitters that were probably not encrypted, so probably a code is used so that the other side would not find out in an unauthorised way what was going on. And I'm not denying that a map existed, but I'm talking about map extracts for police action in anti-terrorist activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that kind of extract can be found somewhere in some MUP archives, a map extract of this kind that was sent to the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about activities or codes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, no, what you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coded map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers not overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that it was -- well, it was in the units. Now, whether somebody actually stored that at the ministry as well, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Regarding the transcript, I apologise to my colleague Aleksic. The witness said that we cannot find it in the MUP staff because it was distributed further, and that part is missing completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you say that, Mr. Mijatovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I wasn't following this very attentively, the question, I'm sorry. Could you please repeat it once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic says that you said you cannot find it, which I think is a map extract, in the MUP staff because it was distributed further, that part is missing completely -- sorry, did you say that you cannot find the map extract in the MUP staff because it was distributed further?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood the question. Yes, yes, it cannot be found for the following reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's all we need to know at the moment. If anyone wants to explore it further, they will. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, yesterday on page 79 while responding to the Prosecutor's question -- well, actually what he put to you was that none of the tasks that were prescribed in that decision on the establishment of the staff was not carried out by you -- or not you, the staff. But then you said that the reason for that was the fact that the plan had been adopted, the minister and his assistants were present, and after that Generals Stevanovic and Djordjevic came to Pristina and that Djordjevic informed the police officers about that plan and that police units should take part in these activities. And you said practically this was approval and at the same time his order, "naredjenje," that units start anti-terrorist actions together with the units of the Army of Yugoslavia. Am I right? Is that what you said roughly?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot repeat each and every word that I said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just stop. Where you're both speaking the same language, there has to be a gap between the question and the answer to allow the interpretation to catch up. Secondly, Mr. Aleksic, what is your question? You know, this is the sort of repetition that's unnecessary, I imagine, for the purpose. What -- just ask the question that you want to ask. After all, it's a privilege that you're being allowed to have this further cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Your Honour. I have understood this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, could General Djordjevic command the JSO unit?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said that as far as I know that never happened. Now, whether he had some kind of special authorisation from the minister because the minister was the superior of both sectors, state security and public security, well I don't know. He was chief of the public security sector. I cannot put questions like that to him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's enough. We don't want speculation. You can't answer it. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, yesterday on page 78 of the transcript you said, in response to the Prosecutor's questions, that orders with the heading Joint Command March and April 1999 were based on a plan that you talked about earlier on in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have once again P2166, page 2 in Serbian and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And could you just read out this one sentence for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't read it. Just ask your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that this plan of -- this anti-terrorist plan, whatever it was called, and no matter how many stages it involved, that action according to this plan was carried out from the end of July until the end of September and that that was stated, that the plan was over, the actions were over. Is this stated in this document dated the 29th of October?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's a quite unnecessary question. If the document says it, it says it; and it doesn't matter whether the witness says it says it or not. If there's a question about his own personal knowledge, then put that question to him, but don't ask him to state the obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. By your leave, a few questions were raised, first of all, the presence of my client at this meeting on the 22nd of July, 1999 [as interpreted], and the second question has to do in part to what Mr. Aleksic asked about and it has to do with this significance -- significant difference in the witness's statements in terms of planning from the corps and the answers that I got in cross-examination and the response that the Prosecutor [as interpreted] gave you and the Prosecutor, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll allow you to deal with the first matter but not the second. That's been explored by both of you already.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honour, just one document which I feel is both in the interests of justice and in the interests of what happened in late July 1998 in the MUP staff and I think many things will become clearer, both for the Chamber and for the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why didn't you show him the document when you were dealing with the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I was satisfied with his response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I repeat, we will allow you to deal with the first and not with the second. You can tell us what the document is in the second matter, but that's all. We are -- there's got to be proper control over these proceedings. You have to think ahead in your cross-examination to what you need to deal with, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I am doing my best to be as efficient as possible. The second document is the minutes of the staff of the 29th of July, 1998, only seven days after the meeting of the 22nd of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is there a passage in it you wish to draw your attention to?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 1, the words of General Sreten Lukic. The document is marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you may proceed with your questions about the attendance of Mr. Lazarevic at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Further cross-examination by Mr. Cepic:

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, it's me again. You mentioned that on the 22nd of July most probably Pavkovic and Lazarevic attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said "probably" because I didn't have the minutes before me. I really cannot remember so many facts and so much data, who was where at what time, what they said precisely. I'm not a computer. That's why I said "probably." I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you aware that at that period General Lazarevic was in Djakovica at the forward command post of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible, but I really can't remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, how on earth could you expect him to answer that? This is a situation where if a point has to be put then it should be, but this is not a general reopening of cross-examination even on this point. Now, if you have a question that this witness can answer that will resolve this, ask him it; but bear in mind that he appears not to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm satisfied with his responses, Your Honour, and I have no further questions about my first topic. However, I ask for leave to show the document I mentioned because many things would be clarified to all sides in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, was he present at the meeting on the 29th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, that -- we're satisfied that we can read the document and deal with it, what Mr. Lukic says in the document, Mr. Cepic. Mr. Lukic, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here I am again. We have made you work very hard, both during the proofing and now, but there's still something we have to clarify at the end. So I'll start with what we did today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have on e-court P1693, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you still have those files?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Those binders, that is. P1693, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find 1693 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, in that case, we'll look at it on the monitor. I wanted to speed things up, but obviously it's not helping. So this is an overview of events of significance for security. It's for the Kosovo and Metohija staff, so first of all, Mr. Hannis asked you about this number. He asked you about the number of 12A, so in the case of this document I'll only ask you the following: For the sake of the record, is it correct that in front of the word "number" there's no number here?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the number following the word "number," is that the number of the document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As I need to deal with something else from this document, we'll come back to the issue of numbers afterwards. Could we now look at the last page of this document, item 4, please. Here we see that it was established that from the 24th of April to the 30th of April, that is, in a space of seven days, a total of 715.158 persons left the territory of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this possible or is it a typographical error? Could this refer to some other period, do you know this?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say with certainty, but here we can see that there is information about the 30th, that's the last day of summary for a previous period, but it would be impossible for this number to have left within a space of five days. This must be from the beginning of the air-strikes. I'm sure this must be some kind of technical error, and in some other document there must be a different date because this looks illogical.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What date should be here instead of the first one?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe from the 4th or from the 20 -- no, no, sorry, from the 24th of March when the air-strikes began, so there must be a typographical error in the month. It must have been the 24th of March, not April.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Tell us -- I mean, I could work out that possibility, anybody could. Tell us your basis for saying that that's what that refers to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, because you can see that there is a figure only for the 30th and then there's a summary, and it would be logical to have a summary from only the past five days not the entire period from the beginning of the air-strikes to the 30th of April. So this must have referred to all the days when there were movements of civilians. That's why I assume it must be an error, but it can probably be checked by looking at other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says here, Your Honours, "in total," but we leave this and clarify it on some other occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, I'd like to ask you the following in connection with this information. Was there ever an attempt to conceal the number of people leaving Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nor was there any reason to conceal it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the regular daily reports, were the figures received from the organizational units on the ground included?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had no other sources, so it only came from the daily reports of the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And was this forwarded to the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These reports were put together, collated, and then forwarded to the ministry in Belgrade. But as I said previously, the secretariats sent these reports in parallel, both to the ministry and the staff. So the ministry would have received these reports from another source also.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have in e-court Exhibit 6D253.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When it shows up on the screen, I am not interested in the contents of the document, Mr. Mijatovic. I only want to concentrate on the number. So this document is just an example on which we can see something about the number. Does this document after the word "number" also contain a figure?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's 223-90, that is the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And to the left of the word "number" we have 12A?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that the number you were referring to when you said that that was the number of the MUP staff on -- in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that 12 was the number referring to the police administration and the headquarters of the ministry and that A had been added to indicate that it was a staff document because the staff did not have its own number in the system. I don't know what it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Today on page 13, line 18, my learned friend Mr. Hannis asked you how many years had elapsed from the point in time when the staff was established to the point of time when it was transformed from a temporary to a permanent body. And your reply was that this never happened. After that my learned friend asked you, as evidently he had not received the response he had wished for, he asked you whether you were a legal expert and you said you were not. My question is the following. Does the fact that you are not a legal expert prevent you, in view of the position you held, from knowing that this was not an organizational unit of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's quite clear that the staff was never an organizational unit of the MUP, and one of the proofs of that is that each time a new staff was formed, a document would have to be issued, a decision; and had it been a permanent body this would not have been necessary. According to the rules, it did not exist as a permanent organizational unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see in e-court Exhibit P1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have that document. It's a staff minutes of the 7th of May, 1999, and my learned friend asked you about this document today. I would only like to see in e-court page 8. We see here on the top third of the page that it was Major-General Ilic Dragan's turn to speak. Can you please tell us, if you remember, why Major-General Dragan Ilic submitted a report at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can remember, in view of the chiefs of the secretariats being present there, he informed them why he came to Pristina, what was his assignment, what was he doing, and I cannot read all of this, but as far as I know, he reported on a meeting held with the chiefs of the criminal police departments of the SUP, secretariats of Kosovska Mitrovica, about what needed to be done to improve the efficacy of the work; and he also stated that a plan was made to clear the terrain and that the plan was distributed to the OKP chiefs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now put Exhibit 5D1417 on e-court. The document has not been translated, but it was used by my colleague Mr. Cepic in his cross-examination. It's a document titled: "The deployment of the PJP in the theatre on the 17th of April, 1999."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You cannot see from this document what its source is and you cannot see who actually drafted the document, so I'm not going to ask you to speculate on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that this was a leading question and the witness already provided relevant information in relation to this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No question's been asked, so there's nothing to adjudicate on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, I apologise, Your Honour. Not a question -- the question as such, but the witness has been provided with arguments or argumentation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's impossible to determine that until we know what the question is, so let's hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was not aware that the witness mentioned the source of the document at all or that he said who signed it, but if he did, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In any case, there were quite a lot of problems when you were asked who was the commander of the unit who decided who would substitute for the commander if the commander was not in the field. I think these questions will be resolved during the proceedings, but I would like to ask you this. Under 1 it actually says in the Cyrillic I, if it was the Latin alphabet it would be an E, it says the 36th Detachment and then under --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You'll need to repeat the question for the interpreter, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat my question, Mr. Mijatovic. I think that I spoke too quickly. At the top of the page below the heading it says "I" in the Cyrillic, a capital "I" in the Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The secretariat in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then under this heading, in the third group, the line begins with the number 3, and it says: "The 122nd Intervention Brigade." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see this on the screen so we don't have to move anything. At the bottom we see three letters I in the Cyrillic. If it was in the Roman alphabet we would have the Roman III, and it says secretariat in Pec. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under number 1 we also see where it says 122nd Intervention Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude from this document, if the document is correct, that the 122nd Intervention Brigade, whenever this document was drafted, and this is allegedly the 17th of April, 1999, that the 122nd Brigade was divided in two sections or two parts --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is evident --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't answer that. That is an utterly leading question. It's rather obvious the answer, in which case the whole question has been unnecessary. There's no point at telling the witness the answer at this stage in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Move to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hypothetical question: If the brigade were to be divided in two parts, would each part have its own commander?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would. Somebody would have to lead those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware if in practice it ever happened that one detachment was divided into several parts or into two parts, and are you aware if each of those parts then had to have its own commander?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for example, if the detachment has six companies and is divided into two parts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, no, give us a specific example. That's what you're being asked. You've been asked about your personal knowledge; give us an example of where that happened. Name the detachment and, if you can, the commanders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at this point I couldn't tell you about any specific examples, but I know that the dispatch on deployment, it would happen that three companies would send -- be sent to an assignment, the other three would be resting. So one section would be on assignment, the others would be resting. Also, those heading those companies would also need to rest. The commander was unable to go all the time. We would either be substituted by his deputy or by some assistant or somebody from the company command so that the commander could rest, but somebody had to lead or head each of those parts whenever it was out on an assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I continue, Your Honour? I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. But your question hasn't been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If the witness doesn't know, he doesn't know. I tried. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to see on the ELMO -- on the e-court Exhibit 4D406, please. This is a text from the Politika daily. Can we please look at the two middle shorter columns at the top of the page. Can we zoom in on that part. Do you have 4D406 in your binder, please, but maybe it might be too -- the print might be too small?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know whether I have it, but perhaps we can zoom in on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you read it now?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Maybe if we can move it to the left. It's too large now so I don't see the entire part. Maybe we can reduce it a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see it now.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this part, but I don't know which part you will be putting your question from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The middle column beginning with the words: "Concurrently with or along with ..." Can you please read, it's not a long text, can you please read both paragraphs in this middle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have we not have this read already?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or you can read it to yourself just to see what it's about and then I will put questions to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But did we not have this already in your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Aleksic asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. What's your question. The witness must know what it says if he's been asked about it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This article mentions the number of arrested persons and it says that several hundred are in question, from what I can remember, and then in the lower paragraph it says that the state organs are acting in accordance with the law and impartially, although the military courts had already passed down a large number of punishments or sentences. I would like to ask you if you can tell us, to which structures do these persons belong, the persons that are being referred to, thus criminals who have already been discovered?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first and the second paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was mentioned during the reports at -- at the meetings with the chief of the secretariat, and also the reports said that the perpetrators of crimes were practically from all structures, both from the active and reserve forces of both the army and the police and from among the ranks of the civilians. So I cannot speak about the percentages or any specific number, but I know that the perpetrators from all structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you something now that was also the subject of some questioning. Sometimes we lawyers put strange questions, if I may say so. Did the MUP headquarters ever command or lead the military territorial detachments or units of the civilian defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you permit me, this question does not arise from the cross-examination because nobody actually touched upon the military territorial units or composition. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But there was a document I think introduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like to go back again to the participation of some units of the PJP, so again I'm going to put a hypothetical question to you. If a company, for example, from the composition of the 124th Brigade were to take part in an anti-terrorist action with the Army of Yugoslavia, would that also unit get the same extract from the map just as the PJP units got that, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean if it participated independently?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. If it participated not as a detachment but as a company from the detachment or the brigade, if it participated in a joint anti-terrorist action with the military of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was participating independently, it would need to get the map because that would be the most basic document on the basis of which it would be acting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next topic you were asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't understand. I didn't understand the question. It may be a translation problem, but is the 124th Brigade you're referring to a MUP brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It says: "Would that unit also get the same extract from the map just as the PJP units got?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: PJP detachments it should be in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you're asking whether the 124th Brigade would get the same sort of documentation as the PJP unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Because they had a PJP unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right. I asked about the smaller units, if the smaller units, for example, on the level of the company is included into the plan separately, not with the whole detachment or brigade, would that company receive the same documents as the brigade or detachment receives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do you understand the answer to be? The question becomes clear, I see that, but what does the answer mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that the answer is affirmative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: They would get the same map? Because the answer was originally no. If you're content then you can move on, but I find it difficult to understand. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I keep standing up, but I understood the answer as the witness's assumption not as something definite.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We understood that the witness said yes to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, the no is part of the question, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you understand the answer to be it's the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can -- can you clarify. I don't want to be -- to lead this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, just carry on. I'm now -- the explanation's sufficient for me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During cross-examination you were asked about the RPO or the reserve police sectors. I am going to ask you this: Do you know when they were founded; and if you do, these RPOs, reserve police stations, and when they stopped existing as such?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when they were established, I don't know the date, but as far as I know these RPOs were established before I arrived at Pristina, and they stopped functioning when the mobilisation began just before the war broke out when members of those stations went to their war units because they were all from the reserve forces of the police and the army. Maybe someone stayed in the villages, I don't know for what reasons, but the stations as such were dismantled.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next topic. Did the Ministry of Internal Affairs in any of its documents provide that the MUP staff in Pristina, the staff -- the MUP staff in Pristina from it establishment onwards in 1990 had to have its own war plan?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor asked you about the KVM reporting back on actions and this was on the basis of your written statement. Was it enough for the KVM to be informed about an action at the local level, an anti-terrorist or any other type of action?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quite sufficient since they had their own organized centres in that area. Activities were conducted in that area, they had MUP officer and somebody from the communications centre. So they were able to follow on the basis of these officers, including the liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that case, do you have to inform them specifically personally if they had already been informed at local level?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no need for that, although very often I did that too, but now I cannot claim that I did that in each and every situation, but often I did that so there was this double-track information. They were informed at the highest level in Kosovo and Metohija and also at local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was there a segment about which you personally had to inform the KVM?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about movements of units or some activities, if they involve a larger area, two or three secretariats namely, then I'd have to, two or three secretariats within the province, then it was my duty to inform the KVM in Pristina about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My colleague Mr. Hannis asked you about the Jaskevo action -- Jeskovo, sorry, did you personally inform the members of the OSCE about this and were they informed at all about this action of the army and the police? At that moment you could not remember the specific occurrence, and now I'm going to show you Exhibit 5D112; and could it please be called up in e-court. It's obvious that the document is only in English. This is a report of the Kosovo Verification Mission for the 11th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 2 on the screen, paragraph 4 is at the very top of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since this is a document in English, I'm going to read out this paragraph in English so that you would get the right translation of that, and it is important in order to clarify Mr. Hannis's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is going to be your question at the end of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question would be that this witness particularly informed OSCE about that action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And he said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- remember at that time because I didn't show him this document. It was in English, and we skipped this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or maybe it's better idea if the translators read this in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, he -- you read it in English --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- and they will translate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Number 4: "Security situation. "Security forces conducted a joint operation against the KLA in Jeskovo (south-west of Prizren). The VJ deployed in Hoca Zagradska, Blusa, and Bijac. Approximately eight tanks with armoured personnel carriers, artillery, and" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There is a sentence about the deputy chief of police in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Oh, you want me to read just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do we need to even ask him the question. The KVM have reported that he -- and you've clarified the point and you've dealt with Mr. Hannis's matter. Do we need to spend time reading the document when it plainly says what you want to clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want him then to clarify the term used here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, in this document it says: "The deputy chief of police in Kosovo informed OSCE liaison officers that two members of the VJ were also killed," and so on and so forth. [Interpretation] This clumsy term, deputy chief of police in Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This term, the deputy chief of police in Kosovo, and also the term the chief of police in Kosovo, was obviously used by the verification mission. There is no such position. I personally believe that this is a technical error, or rather, their translation. I believe that what they meant was the head of staff or the deputy head of staff, that is the only thing I can say to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember now that you informed about this or not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, often I said that I could not recall all details, dates, names of places, locations, and so on. This shows that they, themselves, say that I informed them, so I see that from here; but I really cannot recall each and every event myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's get the answer a bit clearer on this, if you're making something of the description which is not clumsy in English. It's a very clear and simple statement of a post that would be recognisable in English. Do you remember reporting this now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we have to read the event. How can he read something I didn't even read?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you not heard enough about it to know whether you reported it? Do you want the whole thing read to you to clarify the position or have you heard enough to tell us whether you remember this incident or not and reported it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot remember each and every incident. I think that Mr. Hannis asked me yesterday about this and I did not remember, and I don't remember even now where this place is; and I do not remember whether I informed the KVM about this or whether this was done at local level. I am not asserting even now, I mean I cannot remember all these details, but from here I see that I did inform them, from this KVM document I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you accept that the deputy chief of police must be you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there would be no one else to inform them from that level because I was deputy head of staff in charge of coordination and cooperation with them. It is me, yes, but this is a clumsy formulation, this is unfortunate wording, but there is no deputy chief of police in Kosovo or is there a chief of police in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Now I would like to call up in e-court Prosecution Exhibit P1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you can see, these are minutes from a meeting of the MUP staff held on the 11th of May, 1999, and I would like to have page 3 on e-court. Number 3, can we see number 3 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, it should be number 6. Can you scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, you were asked about the 86th PJP Detachment and Dragan Obradovic, and what was read out to you was the second bullet point which says: "With the Army of Yugoslavia we did not have any problems but we don't have a particularly good cooperation with them either. We currently do not know where they are or what they are doing." Do you know whether the 86th Detachment of the PJP is a manoeuvre unit or a territorial unit, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the designation of this unit, it is a territorial unit, a territorial detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Territorial units of the PJP, do they take part in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Territorial detachments of the PJP are not trained and sufficiently equipped to take part in such activities because these are highly complex activities and highly risky ones from the point of view of safety and security and they were not prepared for that at that time. I don't know if something was done about that later, but at that point in time no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is their primary task?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their task was after they carry out anti-terrorist activities, because manoeuvre units went to another assignment or on leave, then it was their task to cover this area that had been cleared of terrorists. That was their basic task, that the terrorists do not return there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to have page 6, paragraph 5 of this document. In paragraph 5 we look at bullet point number 1, and what we see is: "Police units are subordinated to the chief of SUP. PJP detachment leaders and police leaders must attend every collegium meeting of the SUP." I would be interested in the following: "Police units are subordinated to the chief of SUP." I'm going to ask you the following now and later on --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, your microphone is on, do you want to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I was curious to know if this is the correct page we have now on the screen. Is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the first line on the top of the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Police units are subordinated to the chief of SUP and ... that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, chiefs of SUPs, or rather, do chiefs of SUPs command PJP units in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They are commanded by their commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask for 5D1418 to be placed on e-court. Later on we're going to go through these pages, but for the record, I first need to refer to certain sections. On the 12th of February, 2008, on page -- transcript page 22198, line 15, I asked you about the reporting of PJP detachments to the staff. However, in that question I highlighted, lest I misinterpret this myself, [In English] "The commanders of the PJP detachments, did they submit reports to you after the actions were completed?" And your answer was at the line 19: "No." [Interpretation] My colleague Mr. Cepic asked you on the 13th of February, 2008, that is to say the day after this, on page 22324, what he asked you was: [In English] "Of course you were receiving reports from all the detachments of the secretariat of the interior, right?" [Interpretation] You answered him as follows inter alia on the next page, that's where the answer starts and the part that we are interested in starts on line 9. [In English] "It was sometimes the case that the detachment commanders would inform the MUP staff as well about the individual developments or if they had come up against the problem. For example, they suffered losses, an action was aborted for some reason, an action was never even launched, there were people who were wounded, they needed help getting them to the hospital, they needed beds to be made available at a hospital, perhaps some other kind of problem, and so on and so forth." [Interpretation] On the 14th of February, 2008, my colleague Mr. Cepic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what's your question? Because all this looks like is a build-up to a very leading question. So can we not have the question and then see if any more is necessary? What you really should be asking, I suspect, is a straightforward, plain, open question to clarify something that you think has been confused by the answers given.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Could we put on e-court page 3 of this document, please. The document has not been translated, and we used it untranslated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, before this document was shown to you, did you say to this chamber that the PJP detachment commanders informed you of the wounded, killed, police fighters and other matters?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That is a leading question; the answer's valueless in re-examination. You could have pointed that out to us where it occurs in the transcript. It's a complete waste of time, but it's your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, I wish to ask you the following: Are you aware what is meant by one in this document, one in brackets and then lightly and then in brackets grey zero, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to the best of my recollection and according to my logic, 1 would mean that one member of the police had been slightly wounded, and then it says grey zero.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So is it correct that the detachment commanders, or rather, did the detachment commanders record to you when a policeman was wounded? Did they also report to you concerning other problems?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but as this man was only slightly wounded it wouldn't happen every time. Only if one was seriously wounded and had to be taken to hospital. I think here it deals more with another problem having to do with the movement of the civilian population and what to do with them, how to accommodate them. That's why he sent this -- in fact, it's a plea for help.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To ask you something else in this connection, this is a dispatch, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says "communique." It's brief, usually we refer to these things as dispatches.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it sent from the ground or from the town; and if town, from what town?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says here it was sent from Podujevo. I assume that in the field an officer would not have the technical possibilities of sending something like this, so he would probably have done it in Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did the detachment commander inform you of this by dispatch? Why didn't he use radio connection?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we said that after the bombing and the destruction of the repeaters the lines or the connections were paralyzed, so he was unable to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now -- [In English] I don't have too much questions left, Your Honour, but I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How long do you reckon -- in fact, it is better if we break at this stage because one matter has come to my attention that I wasn't aware of. Mr. Cepic, when you sought to ask questions about a document, a minute, of the 29th of July, it wasn't -- it wasn't clear to me that the document has not, in fact, been admitted or even marked for identification. Am I right that that is the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And this is 5D1432.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in view of that, my understanding at the time was the document was a production, and the relevant part could be read and that therefore you would be in a position to deal with anything arising in re-examination if you wished. However, it's not part of the record at the moment, so it will be necessary if it is to become part to allow Mr. Cepic to ask the question he wanted to ask. So when we come back, we'll hear what you have to say about that and then see if he is to be allowed to ask a question about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only, Your Honour, if I may, one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It has been uploaded only today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's too late to introduce documents today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we'll hear what you have to say on that when we return. We'll break now for lunch, Mr. Mijatovic. Could you again leave the courtroom with the usher. We'll resume again at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.47 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we do not need to hear from you on this matter. Mr. Cepic, we do not allow any further examination on that document for two reasons, one, for the reason that it was so recently intimated but also because it is not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: However, if you wish to found on it or seek to found on it to any extent, you should include it in the motion for the admission of documents from the bar table which you intend to submit today, and that will give everybody an opportunity to comment on the document before we decide what to do with it. Mr. Lukic can take note of that and if he decides to re-examine on it at this stage then we would probably allow him to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I won't, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, we're getting close to the end. We have had on e-court 5D1418. Could we please have it called up again. Page 2 of this document, please. Do you have the document on your screen, Mr. Mijatovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read this out for me. This is a dispatch of the staff, and who is it sent to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is sent to commander Zivaljevic, commander of the 122nd Intervention Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does it have to do with the previous dispatch? Can we see that or do you need to look at the next page?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see that it is related to that dispatch because I saw that his main problem was the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since it hasn't been translated, could you please read out the first sentence of this text.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Civilian persons should be returned to their villages."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. In these situations was an attempt always made to have civilians returned to their place of residence whenever possible?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the intention coming from the very top, as one would say, from the state leadership, the minister. So the point was that people, civilians, should have as little problems as possible and their main problem was if they were removed from their homes. So an effort was made to have them returned to their homes whenever and wherever possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please read out the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "If that is not feasible, we agree that they be relocated in the positions that you had proposed."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, why would that happen? Why would people nevertheless be put up at other positions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, an alternative it was given here. First of all, if they can return, let them return; but if this could not happen, then people would have to be relocated, put up somewhere, accommodated, provided with food, water, and everything else they needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the last sentence, could you please read that one out. It says thereby --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Therein, ensure action of the police fully in accordance with the law."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why is this being cautioned?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see that from other documents too, the ministry and the staff. What was always pointed out was such questions. For preventive reasons and we also saw that there were various crimes out there and an effort was made not to have this done and that is why we always pointed this out whenever possible to highlight that one should act in accordance with the law and protect the citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to show you one more document in re-direct and that is P1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it please be called up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see this? In order to make it as brief as possible, these are minutes from the MUP staff meeting held on the 21st of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please just have it enlarged a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I would like page 4 to be placed in e-court in the Serbian version and page 7 in English. The bottom of the page in Serbian. You were asked in relation to this paragraph, you see where it says Colonel Miroslav Mijatovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's towards the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's you, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, what is recorded here is what you said. Can you remember this point in time, what it was that you were saying?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I told you, I cannot remember, but when I read this I can see what it is that I said. It's been a very long time, it's hard for me to remember my own words let alone someone else's words.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you read out the middle of the paragraph that starts with the words: "Reports should be ..."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found that sentence. "Reports should be more detailed and contain correct information because based on them we write other reports to the OSCE and the ministry."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you the following, did you always insist on detailed and accurate information to be provided to the OSCE and the ministry?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, we did and we wanted these reports to include as many facts and possible and as much detail as possible so that we could have what we are writing about confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mijatovic. Thank you for your time. Thank you for having testified. No further questions for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, this may sound a naive question, but please treat it as seriously as you possibly can. In three sentences could you tell us what the purpose of the MUP staff for Kosovo being founded was.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As can be seen from this decision, the staff was supposed to do what the decision says; however, when the plan was adopted this decision was derogated, so as we said the staff did not carry out that work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that. So what was the point in having it after that? Can you tell me?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the staff was an auxiliary body of a temporary nature that the minister established for those tasks, as stated in the decision. However, since that was not done then the staff followed the state of security in Kosovo and Metohija and informed the leadership of the ministry about that, provided assistance to organizational units in Kosovo and Metohija when necessary, provided assistance to the units that had been sent out, primarily from a logistical point of view, provided assistance to all the entire police in Kosovo and Metohija when necessary and conveyed the orders of the leadership of the ministry, followed up on the implementation of these tasks and the staff in accordance with the law, and as we have said every authorised official acts in accordance with the law not waiting for any specific orders, "naredjenje," when they thought it was necessary to improve something or to intensify a certain effort we have already said, well, there are orders, "naredjenje," updating the obligations of the members of the police on the ground. And in essence that would be about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what do you mean by providing assistance to organizational units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, when they have a problem, as we saw a few moments ago, the man called and he didn't know what to do with the civilians. He asked for help, assistance, suggestions, and then we said what should be done. When we talked about those plans of combatting terrorism that the secretariats were supposed to work on inter alia, they submitted that to the staff as stated there, well General Stevanovic was there out there too, so from a professional point of view assistance should be provided to them in order to add something on to that if they had left something out, something important, that hadn't been done, so it was along those lines. And also as far as foreigners were concerned, if they had some problems, because we had a man on this staff in relation to these problems because there were quite a number of humanitarian organizations down there and KDOM and KVM and so on and so forth; so if it was necessary to resolve a problem from a professional point of view and others as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you give me an example of assistance which I think you described as logistical assistance.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's part of the assistance. Over these past few days I was saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Give me an example of logistical assistance.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well that's exactly what I wanted to do. For example, a PJP detachment would come out on a task and take a certain amount of ammunition and it would happen that they would spend that ammunition before completing their mission in Kosovo and Metohija, they have nowhere to turn to for supplies, then they ask for assistance through the staff, and then the staff through the ministry submits these requests; and then it is sent down to the unit, that is an example of this kind of logistical support. And secondly if they received some problems in relation to food-supplies, for instance. In Pristina there was a department from the ministry, directly related to the ministry, that had to do with food and accommodation, and through its various points in different secretariats they took care of food-supplies, and then if there were problems with that then we would help through that department to have these things defined properly, or rather, regulated properly so that people would not have a lack of food and water and other things they needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So were you simply a postbox for communications to pass through?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. They had contact with us and this was all put together for all units and sent further up to the ministry so it didn't go individually. Usually several of them would have a problem and then the staff would put all of this together and send it further up to the ministry in order to have this taken care of and to have this assistance provided to the units in terms of what they were lacking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I mean, you had some awfully high-powered people for a postbox.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't have any other people except for those who were there. It's not that we had other people who could do that, I mean lower-ranking ones that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, is there anything arising from that that you wish to take up?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only that you asked Mr. Mijatovic regarding the logistical support.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So there might be, but if you want to explore further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, you may do so -- if you think something arises that you want to take up, then please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I should have asked these questions earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks. Further examination by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, was there other work for which you were not a mere postbox. Can you explain to us what it is the staff did apart from distributing maps and bringing together the requests of the PJPs vis-a-vis Belgrade and also in terms of the KVM?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I didn't say that. When the KVM was there, we intensively had cooperation and contacts every day, and we collected information in relation to what happened and then the KVM was resolving problems and we were resolving problems in relation to that, so that's what I omitted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that complete it or is there something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That completed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I simply observe that the KVM was established sometime after the establishment of this body. Anyway. Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, before the witness leaves I'd like to make just one point, if I could, almost as an amicus curiae, almost as a friend of the Court, and that pertains to this article in Politika, the article of 5 May 1999, 4D406. And, Your Honour, the Trial Chamber had actually ruled on the inadmissibility of this document on 28 November 2007 on the usual -- the well-known ground that it's a newspaper article, not reliable, cannot be admitted for truth of its contents. Now, during this witness's testimony there was reference to it, and I think perfectly properly P2159 was a secretariat -- a Ministry of the Interior report which sent out a copy of the article to the various police units and I think it's legitimate on the question of notice. And then Mr. Fila also brought it up, I think quite legitimately on the question of notice. The only reason I raise it is that Mr. Lukic asked certain questions about the article to the witness, and I don't quarrel with that. I think he's entitled to clarify that area, except he pegged it for the article -- I'd hate to think that this article, a few points of which I say without arguing the point are erroneous, that if it's -- if it goes unchallenged that somehow the Court will accept it as true. I just want to make sure that that's still the law of the case, that 4D406 was rejected as an exhibit on the grounds that it was a newspaper article, could not be introduced for the truth of its contents, but was legitimately introduced for this witness or commented on to the issue of notice to the various police units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have no objections on the proposal of Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think it was Mr. Lukic that actually -- Mr. Aleksic who used it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: Yes, and as I repeat, I think used properly on the question of --
